file_indicators: Presence of 'os.system' calls with destructive arguments in package source code
References to remote payload URLs (e.g., 'http://malicious-remote-url/payload.bin') in source files
Creation and execution of '/tmp/payload.bin' or similar temporary executable files
Modification of file permissions to add execute rights to downloaded files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to suspicious or untrusted domains such as 'malicious-remote-url'
Unexpected downloads of executable files during package import or runtime
Network activity to remote servers immediately upon package import or execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that attempt to execute shell commands with destructive arguments, especially those targeting the root filesystem (e.g., 'rm -rf /'). Flag packages that download and execute remote binaries at runtime, particularly from hardcoded or untrusted URLs. Use endpoint detection and response (EDR) or file integrity monitoring to detect mass file deletions, changes to file permissions, or the creation and execution of suspicious binaries in temporary directories. Network monitoring should alert on outbound connections to known malicious domains or unexpected payload downloads during package import or execution.
